title: What is known about 1RB0LF_0LC1LB_0RD1LA_1RE0RA_---1RD_1RC1LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_0LC1LB_0RD1LA_1RE0RA_---1RD_1RC1LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its run has a clean, growing left part and an irregular right end. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the halting configurations and no halt in the first 107 steps. The structure described below is observed in simulations, not proved. No halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 44,567 cells have been visited and 36,901 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506).

claims.title: D never reads 0 then 0 (so far)
claims.text: The only halting entry is E reading a 0, and E is entered only from D>0 (write 1, move right): the machine halts exactly when D reads a 0 with a 0 to its right. In the first 108 steps E is entered 8,152,495 times, always onto a 1.

claims.title: A growing left part and an irregular right end
claims.text: At the left end in state F the tape reads alternately F>0 0 (1011)^77 1 (101110)^n 1010 (111011)^m … and F>0 0 (1011)^77 1010 (111011)^n (1)^5 (011101)^m …, with n growing by about one per two round trips (n = 296 at step 2,896,194, 2017 at step 81,421,812). Beyond the counter m, 20 to 60 cells at the right end change irregularly from trip to trip; the middle counter m (23 at step 3·106, 17 at 8·107, 16 at 7·108, its 6-cell word rotating as the phase changes) loses a block now and then.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The left part is regular, but the right end is an irregular region with no visible period: a proof needs a description of that region (perhaps as a finite set of words the head keeps rewriting, a closed-language argument), and the slow loss of the counter m suggests a long-term change of regime when m reaches 0, which has not been observed yet.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine sweeps back and forth over a tape that grows by about one cell per trip on each side. The left part is a neat stack of 6-cell blocks; the right end is a small region that comes out different every time the head visits it. That region is the open part.

facts.text: No halt, checked by Lean's kernel (10<sup>7</sup> by compiled code).
No halt in the C simulator.
Both ends grow like the square root of the step count.

sections.heading: The one way to halt
html: The only halting entry is E reading a 0. E is entered only from D reading a 0 (D writes 1 and moves right), so the machine halts exactly when D>0 0 occurs: D on a 0 with a 0 to its right. In the first 108 steps D reads a 0 8.15 million times, and the next cell has always been a 1. For example the window around the head when E is entered is 101[1]011 or 111[1]110 nearly every time (c/haltwatch.c).

sections.heading: The left part: a stack of blocks
html: Stop the simulator whenever the head reaches a new cell at the left end. From step 758,518 on the tape alternates between two shapes:

The second is the first one with the long block shifted by two cells: the round trip that takes one to the other moves the boundary 1010 through the whole block. n grows by one about every two trips: n = 296 at step 2,896,194, 297 at 2,910,839, 517 at 7,018,812, 2017 at 81,421,812. Since each trip crosses the whole tape, n grows like the square root of the step count.
The block (1011)^77 at the far left is built in an earlier phase (steps 75,000 to 150,000, when a first block of 101110s of length about 48 is converted into it) and is not touched after that.

sections.heading: The right end: irregular
html: Behind the counter (111011)^m (or (011101)^m, depending on the phase) the last few dozen cells differ from one visit to the next. Three consecutive left-end samples:

The middle counter itself shrinks now and then (its word is a rotation of 111011 or of 101110, depending on where the phase is): 24 blocks at step 400,000, 23 at 3·106, 20 at 7·106, 17 at 8·107, 16 from 7·108 to at least 109 (n = 7166 at step 952,948,534): the losses get rarer. What happens when it reaches 0 has not been seen. Both a non-halting proof and a halting run would come from this region; nothing about it is proved.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506).
After 109 steps the tape spans 44,567 cells (21,740 left of the start, 10,872 right), with a density of 1s of 0.828.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Bouncer whose left part grows by one 6-cell block 101110 every two round trips, in front of a fixed block (1011)^77 and a slowly changing middle counter; the right end is an irregular region that the head rewrites on every visit. No regime proved yet.
family: bouncer with an irregular right end
